Here’s a focused logistics checklist for your December outdoor composting workshop in Madison.

1) Site & shelter
- Confirm exact garden area for:
  - Welcome/sign-in
  - Main demo
  - Kids/family viewing area
- Shelter:
  - Reserve/confirm tent/canopy or existing garden shelter.
  - If possible, have sidewalls or windbreaks (tarps, canvas sides).
- Ground:
  - Check for mud/ice.
  - Add mats, pallets, or straw/hay in key standing areas if needed.
- Access:
  - Ensure gate/entrance is unlocked and easy to find.
  - Confirm restroom access and how to direct people there.

2) Weather & comfort
- Weather checks:
  - Re-check forecast 3–5 days before and again the morning of.
  - Decide “move to Dec 21” criteria (e.g., heavy rain, ice, dangerous windchill).
- Comfort:
  - In promo, tell people to dress in warm layers and sturdy shoes/boots.
  - If possible, provide:
    - Hot water/tea/cocoa station.
    - A wind-sheltered corner near the demo.
- Lighting:
  - Ensure adequate daylight in your chosen spot 1–3 pm.
  - Optional: simple battery lanterns/strings if it’s very overcast.

3) Composting/demo materials
- Compost system:
  - At least one functioning bin/pile as main demonstration.
  - Browns: dry leaves, shredded paper/cardboard, straw.
  - Greens: fruit/veg scraps, coffee grounds, fresh plant material.
- Tools & containers:
  - Pitchfork, shovel, hand trowels.
  - Buckets or tubs for transporting greens/browns to the demo area.
  - Watering can or hose (if accessible) for moisture demo.
- Visual aids:
  - Simple posters or boards showing:
    - Browns vs greens (with examples).
    - “Yes/No” list of items.
    - Basic recipe (e.g., 2–3 parts browns : 1 part greens).
  - Optional: clear tub or small bin for close-up layering demo.
- Cleanliness:
  - Gloves (adult + a few kid sizes).
  - Hand sanitizer or hand-wash access.
  - Rags/paper towels for quick clean-ups.

4) Participant experience & flow
- Layout:
  - Welcome/sign-in/info table near entrance.
  - Demo area with semicircle of standing space and a few chairs.
  - Kid-friendly viewing spot where they can see but not crowd tools.
- Timing (simple run-of-show):
  - 0–10 min: Welcome, goals, quick overview.
  - 10–30 min: Compost basics talk + show example bin.
  - 30–75 min: Hands-on building/turning demo with audience participation.
  - 75–105 min: Q&A and troubleshooting common problems.
  - 105–120 min: Wrap-up, resources/handouts, invite to future events.

5) Safety & accessibility
- Safety:
  - Designate a “tool zone” where only adults/assigned helpers use pitchforks/shovels.
  - Keep tools pointed down and stored to the side when not in use.
  - Have a basic first-aid kit on site.
- Accessibility:
  - Check that the path from entrance to demo area is reasonably clear and not dangerously icy.
  - Provide a few chairs/benches for people who need to sit.
  - Use large, high-contrast print on any key signs or info boards.

6) Signage & wayfinding
- External:
  - Sign at garden entrance: “Outdoor Composting Workshop – 1–3 pm.”
  - Arrows from parking/bus stop to gate and workshop area.
- On-site:
  - Labels for:
    - “Browns”
    - “Greens”
    - “Finished Compost”
    - “Active Pile”
  - Optional station signs: “Welcome,” “Demo Area,” “Kids’ Spot.”

7) Handouts & take-home resources
- Handouts:
  - One-page “How to Start Composting at Home” including:
    - What to compost.
    - Basic layering and turning guidance.
    - Simple troubleshooting (smell, pests, too wet/dry).
    - Your org name + contact/site.
- Digital:
  - Optional QR code linking to:
    - A PDF guide.
    - Your website or sign-up for future events.

8) Staffing & roles
- People:
  - Lead facilitator (teaching).
  - 1–2 helpers for:
    - Welcome/sign-in and directions.
    - Managing tools/materials.
    - Keeping kids safely engaged/observing.
- Briefing:
  - Quick pre-event huddle:
    - Who handles late arrivals.
    - Who answers logistics questions (restrooms, rest, etc.).

action_structured.text:
Here’s a focused logistics checklist for your December outdoor composting workshop in Madison.

1) Site & shelter
- Confirm exact garden area for:
  - Welcome/sign-in
  - Main demo
  - Kids/family viewing area
- Shelter:
  - Reserve/confirm tent/canopy or existing garden shelter.
  - If possible, have sidewalls or windbreaks (tarps, canvas sides).
- Ground:
  - Check for mud/ice.
  - Add mats, pallets, or straw/hay in key standing areas if needed.
- Access:
  - Ensure gate/entrance is unlocked and easy to find.
  - Confirm restroom access and how to direct people there.

2) Weather & comfort
- Weather checks:
  - Re-check forecast 3–5 days before and again the morning of.
  - Decide “move to Dec 21” criteria (e.g., heavy rain, ice, dangerous windchill).
- Comfort:
  - In promo, tell people to dress in warm layers and sturdy shoes/boots.
  - If possible, provide:
    - Hot water/tea/cocoa station.
    - A wind-sheltered corner near the demo.
- Lighting:
  - Ensure adequate daylight in your chosen spot 1–3 pm.
  - Optional: simple battery lanterns/strings if it’s very overcast.

3) Composting/demo materials
- Compost system:
  - At least one functioning bin/pile as main demonstration.
  - Browns: dry leaves, shredded paper/cardboard, straw.
  - Greens: fruit/veg scraps, coffee grounds, fresh plant material.
- Tools & containers:
  - Pitchfork, shovel, hand trowels.
  - Buckets or tubs for transporting greens/browns to the demo area.
  - Watering can or hose (if accessible) for moisture demo.
- Visual aids:
  - Simple posters or boards showing:
    - Browns vs greens (with examples).
    - “Yes/No” list of items.
    - Basic recipe (e.g., 2–3 parts browns : 1 part greens).
  - Optional: clear tub or small bin for close-up layering demo.
- Cleanliness:
  - Gloves (adult + a few kid sizes).
  - Hand sanitizer or hand-wash access.
  - Rags/paper towels for quick clean-ups.

4) Participant experience & flow
- Layout:
  - Welcome/sign-in/info table near entrance.
  - Demo area with semicircle of standing space and a few chairs.
  - Kid-friendly viewing spot where they can see but not crowd tools.
- Timing (simple run-of-show):
  - 0–10 min: Welcome, goals, quick overview.
  - 10–30 min: Compost basics talk + show example bin.
  - 30–75 min: Hands-on building/turning demo with audience participation.
  - 75–105 min: Q&A and troubleshooting common problems.
  - 105–120 min: Wrap-up, resources/handouts, invite to future events.

5) Safety & accessibility
- Safety:
  - Designate a “tool zone” where only adults/assigned helpers use pitchforks/shovels.
  - Keep tools pointed down and stored to the side when not in use.
  - Have a basic first-aid kit on site.
- Accessibility:
  - Check that the path from entrance to demo area is reasonably clear and not dangerously icy.
  - Provide a few chairs/benches for people who need to sit.
  - Use large, high-contrast print on any key signs or info boards.

6) Signage & wayfinding
- External:
  - Sign at garden entrance: “Outdoor Composting Workshop – 1–3 pm.”
  - Arrows from parking/bus stop to gate and workshop area.
- On-site:
  - Labels for:
    - “Browns”
    - “Greens”
    - “Finished Compost”
    - “Active Pile”
  - Optional station signs: “Welcome,” “Demo Area,” “Kids’ Spot.”

7) Handouts & take-home resources
- Handouts:
  - One-page “How to Start Composting at Home” including:
    - What to compost.
    - Basic layering and turning guidance.
    - Simple troubleshooting (smell, pests, too wet/dry).
    - Your org name + contact/site.
- Digital:
  - Optional QR code linking to:
    - A PDF guide.
    - Your website or sign-up for future events.

8) Staffing & roles
- People:
  - Lead facilitator (teaching).
  - 1–2 helpers for:
    - Welcome/sign-in and directions.
    - Managing tools/materials.
    - Keeping kids safely engaged/observing.
- Briefing:
  - Quick pre-event huddle:
    - Who handles late arrivals.
    - Who answers logistics questions (restrooms, rest, etc.).
    - Who takes photos (if appropriate and with consent).

9) Contingency & backup date (Dec 21)
- Before Dec 14:
  - Set a firm decision time for weather call (e.g., by noon the day before).
  - Have a ready-to-use “We’re moving to Dec 21” message for:
    - Email list.
    - Social media.
    - Website/event listings.
- If you move to Dec 21:
  - Update the description/title of the Dec 14 calendar event to reflect that it’s postponed.
  - Update the Dec 21 backup event to be the official date and match all public listing details.

If you’d like, next I can:
- Turn this into a short internal checklist for volunteers (with bullet tasks and timing), or
- Help you write the public event description/promo text you’ll post and email out.

Here’s a promo package you can use for email and social.

Email version

Subject line options (pick one)
- Learn to Compost Outdoors – Community Workshop at the Garden (Dec 14)
- Turn Food Scraps into Soil: Outdoor Composting Workshop in Madison
- Free Outdoor Composting Workshop – Community Garden, Dec 14

Email body
Outdoor Composting Workshop at the Community Garden  
Sunday, December 14, 2025 · 1:00–3:00 pm  
Location: Community Garden, Madison (outdoors, with a covered area)

Join us for a hands-on outdoor composting workshop designed for families and community members. We’ll cover the basics of turning your food scraps and yard waste into healthy soil, even in Wisconsin’s colder months.

During this 2-hour workshop, you’ll learn:
- What can and can’t go into a compost pile  
- How to balance “browns” and “greens” so your pile breaks down properly  
- Simple ways to manage moisture, airflow, and winter conditions  
- How to avoid common problems like smell, pests, and soggy piles  
- How to start (or improve) a home compost setup with the space you have

What to expect:
- Outdoor, hands-on demos at the community garden  
- Kid- and family-friendly explanations and chances to help (with safe tasks)  
- Time for your specific questions and troubleshooting  
- Take-home tips so you can get started right away

What to bring:
- Weather-appropriate layers and sturdy shoes or boots  
- Optional: a small container of food scraps (vegetable/fruit scraps, coffee grounds) to add to the demo pile  
- Any compost questions or challenges you’d like help with

This workshop is free and open to the public.

Questions? Contact: vanessa.martinez@caedpolicy.org

Note: This is an outdoor event. We’ll use a basic covered area/tent as needed for shelter. In case of severe weather, we may shift the workshop to the following Sunday afternoon; updated information will be shared via email and social channels if that happens.

Dress for the weather and bring your compost questions!  
Details: Sunday 12/14 · 1–3 pm · Community Garden, Madison.

Learn what to compost, how to build a healthy pile (even in winter), and get your questions answered. Free + family-friendly, open to all.

Option 3 (story / quick post)

Join our free Outdoor Composting Workshop at the Community Garden (Madison)  
🗓 Sunday, Dec 14, 2025  
🕐 1:00–3:00 pm  
Open to all ages and experience levels—come dressed for the weather!

If you tell me your main channel (newsletter platform, Instagram, Facebook, etc.), I can tweak the length and tone for that specific use.</action>
